item.title: A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Complete TE/TM Separability in Fully Anisotropic Waveguides
item.description: arXiv:2611.17888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A necessary and sufficient condition is established for complete transverse-electric/transverse-magnetic (TE/TM) separability in waveguides homogeneously filled with a fully anisotropic and lossless medium. The permittivity and permeability tensors are Hermitian positive-definite and may contain nonzero transverse--longitudinal coupling terms. Complete TE/TM separation occurs if and only if the transverse permeability block is proportional to the transpose of the transverse permittivity block and the corresponding transverse--longitudinal coupling vectors satisfy the same proportionality relation after complex conjugation. The longitudinal constitutive entries remain independent apart from positive definiteness. The condition is derived directly from the source-free Maxwell equations, and independent analyses of the TE and TM modes lead to the same material relation. Since no boundary condition enters the derivation, the criterion is independent of the boundary type. Full-vector waveguide mode analyses using our in-house programs for perfect-electric-conductor and Bloch-periodic waveguides, with material tensors satisfying and violating the condition, agree with the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Wei Jiang, Jie Liu

item.title: A Concise Introduction to Quantum Electromagnetics
item.description: arXiv:2611.17988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This book introduces quantum electromagnetics to readers trained in classical electromagnetics, without assuming a systematic background in quantum mechanics. The central question is when classical descriptions suffice, and when the quantum states of matter or the field must be retained explicitly. Starting from familiar electromagnetic modes and material response, the discussion develops atomic dynamics, field quantization, and the interaction of quantized fields with quantum matter. Particular attention is given to how mode profiles, Green functions, and scattering matrices obtained from classical electromagnetic calculations enter quantum models. Atomic coherence, photon statistics, spontaneous emission, and cavity coupling are developed through derivations that identify the physical assumptions and limits of each description. Examples drawn from atomic clocks, Rydberg-atom receivers, and single-photon devices connect these concepts to excitation, propagation, and measurement in practical systems. Loss and noise are included in relating internal dynamics to measured signals and correlations. The final discussion examines how sensitivity and claims of quantum advantage depend on bandwidth, measurement resources, and the classical reference used for comparison. The aim is to help readers choose an appropriate model, carry out the calculation, and understand what its predictions mean for an electromagnetic measurement.

item.title: Catenaries in viscous fluid
item.description: arXiv:1509.01282v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work explores a simple model of a slender, flexible structure in a uniform flow, providing analytical solutions for the translating, axially flowing equilibria of strings subjected to a uniform body force and drag forces linear in the velocities. The classical catenaries are extended to a five-parameter family of curves. A sixth parameter affects the tension in the curves. Generic configurations are planar, represented by a single first order equation for the tangential angle. The effects of varying parameters on representative shapes, orbits in angle-curvature space, and stress distributions are shown. As limiting cases, the solutions include configurations corresponding to "lariat chains" and the towing, reeling, and sedimentation of flexible cables in a highly viscous fluid. Regions of parameter space corresponding to infinitely long, semi-infinite, and finite length curves are delineated. Almost all curves subtend an angle less than $\pi$ radians, but curious special cases with doubled or infinite range occur on the borders between regions. Separate transitions in the tension behavior, and counterintuitive results regarding finite towing tensions for infinitely long cables, are presented. Several physically inspired boundary value problems are solved and discussed.
